stem: To study how people travel to work, $100$ workers in city A and $30$ workers in city B were surveyed. Workers in city A: bus $40$, subway $10$, bicycle $50$. Workers in city B: bus $20$, subway $5$, bicycle $5$. The two groups choose independently. If one person is chosen at random from each group, the probability that they travel in the same way is ( )
solution: For each option, multiply the two probabilities of choosing it, then add the results: P(same choice) $= \dfrac{40}{100} \cdot \dfrac{20}{30} + \dfrac{10}{100} \cdot \dfrac{5}{30} + \dfrac{50}{100} \cdot \dfrac{5}{30} = \dfrac{11}{30}$.

stem: A bag contains $4$ red balls and $2$ blue balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. Which of the following statements is correct? ( )
options: The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{8}{15}$
The probability that the two balls have the same colour is $\dfrac{2}{5}$
The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{3}{5}$
The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{4}{15}$
solution: There are $C(6, 2) = 15$ equally likely pairs. “The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{8}{15}$” is correct. There are $4 \cdot 2 = 8$ such pairs out of $15$. “The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{4}{15}$” is incorrect. The pairs are unordered, so there are $8$ such pairs out of $15$ and the probability is $\dfrac{8}{15}$. “The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{3}{5}$” is incorrect. The complement of “at least one red” is “both blue”: $1 - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{14}{15}$. “The probability that the two balls have the same colour is $\dfrac{2}{5}$” is incorrect. That value counts only the red pairs. Adding the blue pairs gives $\dfrac{7}{15}$.

stem: A bag contains $30$ balls of the same size: black, green, yellow and red. When one ball is drawn at random, $P(\text{black}) = \dfrac{1}{5}$, $P(\text{yellow or green}) = \dfrac{8}{15}$ and $P(\text{green or red}) = \dfrac{3}{5}$. Then the probabilities of drawing a green, a yellow and a red ball are, respectively, ( )
solution: The four probabilities add up to $1$. So $P(\text{red}) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{8}{15} = \dfrac{4}{15}$. Then $P(\text{green}) = \dfrac{3}{5} - \dfrac{4}{15} = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and $P(\text{yellow}) = \dfrac{8}{15} - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{5}$. The options use the same three numbers in different orders, so the order green, yellow, red decides the answer.

stem: To study favourite seasons, $40$ teachers and $50$ students were surveyed. Teachers: spring $5$, summer $30$, autumn $5$. Students: spring $15$, summer $20$, autumn $15$. The two groups choose independently. If one person is chosen at random from each group, the probability that they chose different seasons is ( )
solution: For each option, multiply the two probabilities of choosing it, then add the results: P(same choice) $= \dfrac{5}{40} \cdot \dfrac{15}{50} + \dfrac{30}{40} \cdot \dfrac{20}{50} + \dfrac{5}{40} \cdot \dfrac{15}{50} = \dfrac{3}{8}$. So P(different) $= 1 - \dfrac{3}{8} = \dfrac{5}{8}$.

stem: Three people each write down one of the digits $0, 1, \ldots, 9$ at random, independently and with equal probability. The probability that at least two of them write the same digit is ( )
solution: Use the complement "all three are different". Total outcomes: $10^3 = 1000$. All different: $10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 = 720$. So the probability is $1 - \dfrac{720}{1000} = \dfrac{7}{25}$.

stem: A bag contains $4$ blue balls and $2$ black balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. The probability that both balls are blue is ( )
solution: There are $C(6, 2) = 15$ equally likely pairs, and $C(4, 2) = 6$ of them are two blue balls. So the probability is $\dfrac{6}{15} = \dfrac{2}{5}$.

stem: A bag contains $4$ white balls and $2$ blue balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. The probability that the two balls have the same colour is ( )
solution: There are $C(6, 2) = 15$ equally likely pairs. The pairs of the same colour number $C(4, 2) + C(2, 2) = 6 + 1 = 7$. So the probability is $\dfrac{7}{15}$.

stem: A bag contains $4$ black balls and $3$ blue balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. The probability that at least one of the two balls is black is ( )
solution: Use the complement. Pairs with no black ball: $C(3, 2) = 3$ out of $C(7, 2) = 21$. So the probability is $1 - \dfrac{3}{21} = \dfrac{6}{7}$.

stem: To study favourite seasons, $40$ teachers and $100$ students were surveyed. Teachers: spring $25$, summer $5$, autumn $5$, winter $5$. Students: spring $30$, summer $10$, autumn $40$, winter $20$. The two groups choose independently. If one person is chosen at random from each group, the probability that they chose the same season is ( )
solution: For each option, multiply the two probabilities of choosing it, then add the results: P(same choice) $= \dfrac{25}{40} \cdot \dfrac{30}{100} + \dfrac{5}{40} \cdot \dfrac{10}{100} + \dfrac{5}{40} \cdot \dfrac{40}{100} + \dfrac{5}{40} \cdot \dfrac{20}{100} = \dfrac{11}{40}$.

stem: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be the two complex roots of $z^2 - 2z + 2 = 0$, and let $a_n = (z_1^n - z_2^n)^2$. Then $a_2 =$ ( )
solution: The roots are $1 + i$ and $1 - i$, a conjugate pair. Then $z_1^{2} = 2i$ and $z_2^{2}$ is its conjugate, so $z_1^{2} - z_2^{2} = 4i$. Squaring gives $-16$, because $i^2 = -1$.

stem: Which of the following statements about the function $y = 2^x$ is correct? ( )
options: Its graph passes through the origin
Its graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis
Its graph passes through the point $(1, 0)$
solution: “It is monotonically increasing on $\mathbb{R}$” is correct. The base $2$ is greater than $1$, so the function is increasing. “Its graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis” is incorrect. The function is increasing, so $f(-1) \ne f(1)$ and it is not even. “Its graph passes through the origin” is incorrect. At $x = 0$ the value is $1$, not $0$. “Its graph passes through the point $(1, 0)$” is incorrect. At $x = 1$ the value is $2$, not $0$. The point $(1, 0)$ lies on the graphs of logarithmic functions.

stem: An ellipse has a major axis of length $20$ and foci $(\pm 8, 0)$. Its equation is ( )
solution: $2a = 20$ gives $a = 10$, and the foci give $c = 8$. Then $b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = 100 - 64 = 36$. The foci are on the $x$-axis, so $a^2$ goes under $x^2$ and the equation is $\dfrac{x^2}{100} + \dfrac{y^2}{36} = 1$.

stem: A box contains $6$ balls of the same size: $2$ green balls labelled $1, 2$ and $4$ yellow balls labelled $1, 2, 3, 4$. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. The probability that the two balls have different colours and the probability that the sum of their labels is even are, respectively, ( )
solution: There are $C(6, 2) = 15$ equally likely pairs. There are $2 \cdot 4 = 8$ pairs with different colours, so the first probability is $\dfrac{8}{15}$. For the second event, counting the pairs whose labels are both even or both odd gives $\dfrac{2}{5}$.

stem: Three customers each join one of $8$ checkout lines at random, independently and with equal probability. The probability that at least two of them join the same line is ( )
solution: Use the complement "all three are different". Total outcomes: $8^3 = 512$. All different: $8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6 = 336$. So the probability is $1 - \dfrac{336}{512} = \dfrac{11}{32}$.

stem: To study favourite sports, $50$ middle-school students and $100$ university students were surveyed. Middle-school students: football $10$, basketball $15$, badminton $25$. University students: football $30$, basketball $10$, badminton $60$. The two groups choose independently. If one person is chosen at random from each group, the probability that they chose different sports is ( )
solution: For each option, multiply the two probabilities of choosing it, then add the results: P(same choice) $= \dfrac{10}{50} \cdot \dfrac{30}{100} + \dfrac{15}{50} \cdot \dfrac{10}{100} + \dfrac{25}{50} \cdot \dfrac{60}{100} = \dfrac{39}{100}$. So P(different) $= 1 - \dfrac{39}{100} = \dfrac{61}{100}$.

stem: There are $n$ white balls and $n$ red balls, all with distinct labels. From these, $n$ balls are drawn at random without replacement. Let $Q(n)$ be the probability that all $n$ drawn balls have the same colour. Which of the following is correct? ( )
solution: Compute each value by counting: $Q(2) = \dfrac{1}{3}$, $Q(4) = \dfrac{1}{35}$, $Q(5) = \dfrac{1}{126}$. In general $Q(n) = \dfrac{2}{C(2n, n)}$, which decreases as $n$ grows. Hence $Q(2) > Q(4) > Q(5)$.

stem: An ellipse is centered at the origin with its axes on the coordinate axes. Its major axis is three times as long as its minor axis, and it passes through the point $P(0, -3)$. Its equation is ( )
solution: A point on an axis is a vertex, but it can be an end of the major axis or of the minor axis. If it is on the major axis, then $a = 3$ and $b = 1$, which gives $x^2 + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1$. If it is on the minor axis, then $b = 3$ and $a = 9$, which gives $\dfrac{x^2}{81} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1$. Both equations are possible, so an option with only one of them is incomplete.

stem: The graph of the function $f(x) = -3 + \log_a(x - 5)$ ($a > 0$ and $a \ne 1$) always passes through the fixed point ( )
solution: $\log_a 1 = 0$ for every base $a$, so make the expression inside the logarithm equal to $1$: $x - 5 = 1$, so $x = 6$. Then $f(6) = -3 + 0 = -3$ whatever $a$ is. So the fixed point is $(6, -3)$.

stem: The solution set of the inequality $\log_{\frac{1}{3}}(x - 5) < -1$ is ( )
solution: First, the expression inside the logarithm must be positive: $x - 5 > 0$, that is $x > 5$. Next, write $-1 = \log_{\frac{1}{3}} 3$. The base is between $0$ and $1$, so the logarithm is decreasing and the inequality sign reverses: $x - 5 > 3$, that is $x > 8$. Both conditions must hold, so the solution set is $(8, +\infty)$.

stem: Given $a = 2^{0.3}$, $b = \ln 0.5$ and $c = 0.8^{2}$, the order of $a$, $b$, $c$ is ( )
solution: Compare each value with $0$ and $1$. $b = \ln 0.5 < 0$, because the base $e$ is above $1$ and the argument $0.5$ is below $1$. $0 < c = 0.8^{2} < 1$, because a base between $0$ and $1$ raised to a positive power gives a value between $0$ and $1$. $a = 2^{0.3} > 1$, because a base above $1$ raised to a positive power gives a value above $1$. So $b < c < a$.

stem: Let $\boldsymbol{a}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}$ be two non-collinear vectors. If, as vectors, $\overrightarrow{AB} = \boldsymbol{a} + 3\boldsymbol{b}$, $\overrightarrow{BC} = 3\boldsymbol{b} - 5\boldsymbol{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD} = 9\boldsymbol{a} + 9\boldsymbol{b}$, then which three points are collinear? ( )
solution: Three points are collinear when two of the vectors joining them are parallel. $\overrightarrow{BD} = \overrightarrow{BC} + \overrightarrow{CD} = 4\boldsymbol{a} + 12\boldsymbol{b} = 4\overrightarrow{AB}$, so $A$, $B$, $D$ are collinear.

stem: Which of the following statements about logarithms is correct? ( )
solution: $\log_{2}3 > \log_{3}2$ is correct. The left side is greater than $1$, because its argument is greater than its base, and the right side is less than $1$, because its argument is smaller than its base. $\log_{4}2 = \log_{2}4$ is incorrect. The two values are reciprocals of each other: $\log_{4}2 = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\log_{2}4 = 2$. $\lg 2 + \lg 3 = \lg 5$ is incorrect. $\lg 2 + \lg 3 = \lg 6$. The rule is $\lg M + \lg N = \lg(MN)$, not $\lg(M + N)$. $\log_{\frac{1}{2}}4 = 2$ is incorrect. $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{-2} = 4$, so the value is $-2$.

stem: On the complex plane, the point representing a non-real complex number $z$ lies on the line $y = 2x$. If $z$ is a root of the equation $x^2 + mx + 40 = 0$ ($m \in \mathbb{R}$), then $m =$ ( )
solution: The coefficients are real, so the other root is $\bar{z}$. Write $z = t + 2ti$, since $z$ lies on $y = 2x$. The product of the roots is $z\bar{z} = 5t^2 = 40$, so $t = \pm 2\sqrt{2}$. The sum of the roots is $z + \bar{z} = 2t = -m$. Hence $m = \pm 4\sqrt{2}$, with both signs possible because $t$ can be positive or negative.

solution: Use the complement "all three are different". Total outcomes: $9^3 = 729$. All different: $9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7 = 504$. So the probability is $1 - \dfrac{504}{729} = \dfrac{25}{81}$.

stem: Which of the following statements about the function $y = 2^x$ is correct? ( )
options: Its graph passes through the origin
Its graph passes through the point $(1, 0)$

Every power of a positive base is positive, so the function never takes the value $0$ or a negative value. “Its graph passes through the point $(1, 0)$” is incorrect. At $x = 1$ the value is $2$, not $0$. The point $(1, 0)$ lies on the graphs of logarithmic functions. “Its graph passes through the origin” is incorrect. At $x = 0$ the value is $1$, not $0$.

stem: The graph of the function $f(x) = a^{2x + 5} + 3$ ($a > 0$ and $a \ne 1$) always passes through the fixed point ( )
solution: $a^0 = 1$ for every base $a$, so make the exponent $0$: $2x + 5 = 0$ gives $x = -\dfrac{5}{2}$. Then $f\left(-\dfrac{5}{2}\right) = a^0 + 3 = 1 + 3 = 4$ whatever $a$ is. So the fixed point is $\left(-\dfrac{5}{2}, 4\right)$.

stem: The value of $\log_{4}16 - \log_{2}\dfrac{1}{8} + \lg 100$ is ( )
The solution set of the inequality $\lg(x - 3) > 0$ is ( )
solution: First, the expression inside the logarithm must be positive: $x - 3 > 0$, that is $x > 3$. Next, write $0 = \lg 1$. The base is greater than $1$, so the logarithm is increasing and the inequality sign is kept: $x - 3 > 1$, that is $x > 4$. Both conditions must hold, so the solution set is $(4, +\infty)$.

stem: Which of the following statements about the function $y = \log_a x$ ($a > 0$, $a \ne 1$) is correct? ( )
options: Its graph always passes through the point $(0, 1)$
solution: “Its domain is $(0, +\infty)$” is correct. The expression inside a logarithm must be positive. “Its domain is $(-\infty, +\infty)$” is incorrect. The expression inside a logarithm must be positive, so the domain is $(0, +\infty)$. “Its graph always passes through the point $(0, 1)$” is incorrect. $x = 0$ is not in the domain of $y = \log_a x$. The point $(0, 1)$ is the fixed point of $y = a^x$. “When $a > 1$, it is decreasing on $(0, +\infty)$” is incorrect. A logarithm with a base greater than $1$ is increasing.

stem: Regarding the functions $y = x^5$ and $y = \sqrt[5]{x}$, which of the following conclusions is correct? ( )
options: Their graphs are symmetric about the origin
Their graphs are symmetric about the $x$-axis
Their graphs are symmetric about the $y$-axis
Their graphs are symmetric about the line $y = x$
solution: “Their graphs are symmetric about the line $y = x$” is correct. The two functions are inverses of each other, so their graphs are mirror images in the line $y = x$. “Their graphs are symmetric about the $y$-axis” is incorrect. The point $(1, 1)$ lies on $y = x^5$, but its mirror image in the $y$-axis, $(-1, 1)$, does not lie on $y = \sqrt[5]{x}$. “Their graphs are symmetric about the $x$-axis” is incorrect. The point $(1, 1)$ lies on $y = x^5$, but its mirror image in the $x$-axis, $(1, -1)$, does not lie on $y = \sqrt[5]{x}$. “Their graphs are symmetric about the origin” is incorrect. The point $(2, 32)$ lies on $y = x^5$, but its mirror image in the origin, $(-2, -32)$, does not lie on $y = \sqrt[5]{x}$.

stem: Which of the following is correct? ( )
solution: A logarithm $\log_a b$ is positive when $a$ and $b$ lie on the same side of $1$, and negative when they lie on opposite sides. $\log_{0.3}0.2 > 1$ is correct. $y = \log_{0.3} x$ is decreasing because its base is below $1$, and $0.2 < 0.3$, so $\log_{0.3}0.2 > \log_{0.3}0.3 = 1$. $\log_{0.6}7 > 0$ is incorrect. The base $0.6$ is below $1$ and the argument $7$ is above $1$, so the logarithm is negative. $\log_{2}5 < 1$ is incorrect. $y = \log_{2} x$ is increasing and $5 > 2$, so $\log_{2}5 > \log_{2}2 = 1$. $\log_{7}0.6 > 0$ is incorrect. The base $7$ is above $1$ and the argument $0.6$ is below $1$, so the logarithm is negative.

stem: Which of the following inequalities is correct? ( )
solution: In each option the two powers have either the same base, so we use an exponential function, or the same exponent, so we use a power function. $2^{1.2} < 2^{3}$ is correct. Both powers have the base $2$, and $y = 2^x$ is increasing because $2 > 1$. Since $1.2 < 3$, $2^{1.2} < 2^{3}$. $3.2^{2/3} < 1.3^{2/3}$ is incorrect. Both powers have the exponent $2/3$, and $y = x^{2/3}$ is increasing on $(0, +\infty)$ because $2/3 > 0$. Since $1.3 < 3.2$, $1.3^{2/3} < 3.2^{2/3}$. $3.2^{-0.3} > 2.3^{-0.3}$ is incorrect. Both powers have the exponent $-0.3$, and $y = x^{-0.3}$ is decreasing on $(0, +\infty)$ because $-0.3 < 0$. Since $2.3 < 3.2$, $2.3^{-0.3} > 3.2^{-0.3}$. $0.3^{2.25} > 0.3^{2}$ is incorrect. Both powers have the base $0.3$, and $y = 0.3^x$ is decreasing because $0 < 0.3 < 1$. Since $2 < 2.25$, $0.3^{2} > 0.3^{2.25}$.

stem: Let $\boldsymbol{a} = (2, 1)$ and $\boldsymbol{b} = (k, -2)$. If $\boldsymbol{a} \parallel \boldsymbol{b}$, then $k =$ ( )
solution: Parallel vectors satisfy $x_1y_2 - x_2y_1 = 0$: $2 \cdot (-2) - 1k = 0$, so $k = -4$.

stem: In square $ABCD$, let the vectors $\overrightarrow{AB} = \boldsymbol{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD} = \boldsymbol{b}$, and let $F$ be the midpoint of $CD$. Then the vector $\overrightarrow{AF} =$ ( )
solution: Measure every point from $A$: $\overrightarrow{AB} = \boldsymbol{a}$, $\overrightarrow{AD} = \boldsymbol{b}$ and, since $ABCD$ is a parallelogram, $\overrightarrow{AC} = \boldsymbol{a} + \boldsymbol{b}$. Since $F$ is the midpoint of $CD$, $\overrightarrow{AF} = \dfrac{1}{2}(\overrightarrow{AC} + \overrightarrow{AD}) = \dfrac{1}{2}\boldsymbol{a} + \boldsymbol{b}$. So $\overrightarrow{AF} = \dfrac{1}{2}\boldsymbol{a} + \boldsymbol{b}$.

stem: If $|\boldsymbol{a}| = 3$, $|\boldsymbol{b}| = 4$ and the angle between $\boldsymbol{a}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}$ is $120^\circ$, then $|\boldsymbol{a} + 2\boldsymbol{b}| =$ ( )
solution: $\boldsymbol{a} \cdot \boldsymbol{b} = |\boldsymbol{a}||\boldsymbol{b}|\cos 120^\circ = -6$. $|\boldsymbol{a} + 2\boldsymbol{b}|^2 = |\boldsymbol{a}|^2 + 4\boldsymbol{a} \cdot \boldsymbol{b} + 4|\boldsymbol{b}|^2 = 9 - 24 + 64 = 49$, so $|\boldsymbol{a} + 2\boldsymbol{b}| = \sqrt{49} = 7$.

stem: If the complex number $z$ satisfies $z^3 = 1$ and $z \ne 1$, then $1 + z + z^2 + \cdots + z^{50} =$ ( )
solution: Since $z^3 - 1 = (z - 1)(z^2 + z + 1) = 0$ and $z \ne 1$, we get $1 + z + z^2 = 0$. The powers of $z$ repeat every $3$, so every block of three consecutive terms adds up to $0$. The sum has $51$ terms, which is $17$ blocks of three exactly, so the sum is $0$.

stem: If the complex number $z$ satisfies $|z| = 1$, then the minimum value of $|z + 5 + 12i|$ is ( )
solution: The points $z$ lie on the circle with center $0$ and radius $1$, and $|z + 5 + 12i|$ is the distance from such a point to $-5 - 12i$, which is $13$ from the center. The smallest distance is $|13 - 1| = 12$.

stem: A bag contains $12$ balls of the same size: black, green, yellow and red. When one ball is drawn at random, $P(\text{black}) = \dfrac{1}{6}$, $P(\text{yellow or green}) = \dfrac{5}{12}$ and $P(\text{green or red}) = \dfrac{3}{4}$. Then the probabilities of drawing a green, a yellow and a red ball are, respectively, ( )
solution: The four probabilities add up to $1$. So $P(\text{red}) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{6} - \dfrac{5}{12} = \dfrac{5}{12}$. Then $P(\text{green}) = \dfrac{3}{4} - \dfrac{5}{12} = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and $P(\text{yellow}) = \dfrac{5}{12} - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{12}$. The options use the same three numbers in different orders, so the order green, yellow, red decides the answer.

stem: A bag contains $4$ red balls and $5$ yellow balls of the same size. Two balls are drawn at random at the same time. Which of the following statements is correct? ( )
options: The probability that both balls are red is $\dfrac{1}{6}$
The probability that both balls are red is $\dfrac{16}{81}$
The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{5}{6}$
The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{5}{18}$
solution: There are $C(9, 2) = 36$ equally likely pairs. “The probability that both balls are red is $\dfrac{1}{6}$” is correct. There are $C(4, 2) = 6$ such pairs out of $C(9, 2) = 36$. “The probability that at least one ball is red is $\dfrac{5}{6}$” is incorrect. The complement of “at least one red” is “both yellow”: $1 - \dfrac{5}{18} = \dfrac{13}{18}$. “The probability that both balls are red is $\dfrac{16}{81}$” is incorrect. The balls are drawn together, so there is no replacement and the probability is $\dfrac{C(4, 2)}{C(9, 2)} = \dfrac{6}{36} = \dfrac{1}{6}$. “The probability that the two balls have different colours is $\dfrac{5}{18}$” is incorrect. The pairs are unordered, so there are $20$ such pairs out of $36$ and the probability is $\dfrac{20}{36} = \dfrac{5}{9}$.

stem: The coordinates of the foci of the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{4} - \dfrac{y^2}{4} = 1$ are ( )
solution: Unlike an ellipse, a hyperbola has $c^2 = a^2 + b^2$. Here $c^2 = 4 + 4 = 8$, so $c = 2\sqrt{2}$. The foci lie on the axis of the positive term, the $x$-axis, so they are $(\pm 2\sqrt{2}, 0)$.

stem: If the sequence $\{a_n\}$ is $-2, 4, -8, 16, \ldots$, then the general term $a_n =$ ( )
solution: Separate the sign and the size. Size: $2^{n}$. Sign: the first term is negative, so use $(-1)^{n}$. Hence $a_n = (-1)^{n} \cdot 2^{n}$. Check with $n = 1$ and $n = 2$: the formula gives $-2$ and $4$.

stem: The distance from the point $P(4, 0)$ to the point $Q(3, 3)$ is ( )
solution: The coordinate differences are $3 - 4 = -1$ and $3 - 0 = 3$. By the distance formula, $|PQ| = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{1 + 9} = \sqrt{10}$.

stem: Suppose $\cos\alpha = -\dfrac{8}{17}$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{2} < \alpha < \pi$. Then $\sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2} =$ ( )
solution: Find where the half angle lies: $\alpha \in \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)$ gives $\dfrac{\alpha}{2} \in \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, where the sine is positive. $\sin^2\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{1 - \cos\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{1 - \left(-\dfrac{8}{17}\right)}{2} = \dfrac{25}{34}$, so $\sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{34}}{34}$. The interval fixes the sign, so the answer is not $\pm\dfrac{5\sqrt{34}}{34}$.

stem: Given plane vectors $\boldsymbol{a}$, $\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{c}$ with $|\boldsymbol{a}| = 6$, $|\boldsymbol{b}| = 6$, $\boldsymbol{a} \cdot \boldsymbol{b} = -18$ and $\boldsymbol{c} = \lambda\boldsymbol{a} + (1 - \lambda)\boldsymbol{b}$ ($\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$), the minimum value of $|\boldsymbol{c}|$ is ( )
solution: Square it: $|\boldsymbol{c}|^2 = 36\lambda^2 + 2\lambda(1 - \lambda) \cdot (-18) + 36(1 - \lambda)^2$, a quadratic in $\lambda$ that opens upward. Its vertex is at $\lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$, where $|\boldsymbol{c}|^2 = 9$. So the minimum of $|\boldsymbol{c}|$ is $3$.

stem: On the complex plane, the point representing a non-real complex number $z$ lies on the line $y = x$. If $z$ is a root of the equation $x^2 + mx + 18 = 0$ ($m \in \mathbb{R}$), then $m =$ ( )
solution: The coefficients are real, so the other root is $\bar{z}$. Write $z = t + ti$, since $z$ lies on $y = x$. The product of the roots is $z\bar{z} = 2t^2 = 18$, so $t = \pm 3$. The sum of the roots is $z + \bar{z} = 2t = -m$. Hence $m = \pm 6$, with both signs possible because $t$ can be positive or negative.

stem: A week has $7$ days. Three people are chosen at random; each is equally likely to have been born on any day of the week, independently of the others. The probability that at least two of them were born on the same day of the week is ( )
solution: Use the complement "all three are different". Total outcomes: $7^3 = 343$. All different: $7 \cdot 6 \cdot 5 = 210$. So the probability is $1 - \dfrac{210}{343} = \dfrac{19}{49}$.

stem: To study how people travel to work, $60$ workers in city A and $50$ workers in city B were surveyed. Workers in city A: bus $5$, subway $35$, bicycle $20$. Workers in city B: bus $25$, subway $5$, bicycle $20$. The two groups choose independently. If one person is chosen at random from each group, the probability that they travel in different ways is ( )
solution: For each option, multiply the two probabilities of choosing it, then add the results: P(same choice) $= \dfrac{5}{60} \cdot \dfrac{25}{50} + \dfrac{35}{60} \cdot \dfrac{5}{50} + \dfrac{20}{60} \cdot \dfrac{20}{50} = \dfrac{7}{30}$. So P(different) $= 1 - \dfrac{7}{30} = \dfrac{23}{30}$.
